Simulate a binary relapse outcome from relapse counts

Source: R/simulate_binary.R
simulate_binary.Rd

Generate synthetic relapse counts over a common follow-up period with simulate_count(), then define an event when the relapse count exceeds a chosen threshold. The data-generating model and its coefficients are illustrative, not clinical estimates.

Usage

simulate_binary(n = 4000L, seed = 20261114L, followup = 1, threshold = 0L, ...)

Arguments

n

Positive integer sample size. Default is 4,000.

seed

Integer seed, or NULL to use the current random-number state. Supplying a seed sets R's random-number state.

followup

Positive finite common follow-up in years. Default is 1.

threshold

Non-negative integer relapse count above which an event is recorded. The default, 0, defines an event as at least one relapse.

...

Additional arguments to simulate_count(), such as conditional_rr, ps_weights, lp_weights, or dispersion. Do not supply followup_range; follow-up is fixed by followup.

Value

A data frame with the same covariates, treatment and years as simulate_count(), a 0/1 outcome y, and the underlying count relapse_count. A value of 1 means the count exceeds the threshold. Treatment labels are drug0 and drug1.

Details

The binary outcome is fully observed at the common horizon; there is no censoring. A treatment effect on the relapse rate generally implies a different effect on the event probability, depending on follow-up, the threshold, covariates and count distribution. The model does not reconstruct any patient population or individual patient records.

Author

Thomas Debray tdebray@fromdatatowisdom.com

Examples

d <- simulate_binary(n = 500, seed = 1, followup = 1, threshold = 0)
table(d$trt, d$y)
#>        
#>           0   1
#>   drug0 114 110
#>   drug1 152 124
